summary: John Crook worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Southampton, Jesus College, Cambridge under Robert Hinde and William Homan Thorpe, and with Sheng Yen. He held posts at CASBS, Bristol, and Université Bouddhique Européenne.

John D. Dunne specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Amherst, CIHTS under Ram Shankar Tripathi, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Malcolm David Eckel. His career includes posts at CIHTS, Harvard, Emory, and Wisconsin-Madison.

John D. Smith is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London (1975), before becoming University Lecturer in Sanskrit (1984) and Professor (2001–2007) at the University of Cambridge.

John Daido Loori was a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He studied at Rutgers University and under Soen Nakagawa and Taizan Maezumi. He held a post at Naropa University (1974) and served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery (circa 1980–2009).
John Daishin Buksbazen is active in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles and under Taizan Maezumi, Bernie Glassman, and Wendy Egyoku Nakao (attested 2002).

Philosopher John Dewey studied at Burlington High School, the University of Vermont, and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan, the University of Minnesota, the University of Chicago, and Columbia University.

John Dowson was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Edwin Norris. He held positions at the Royal Asiatic Society, East India Company College, Staff College, Camberley (1855–1877), and University College London (1855–1877).

John E. Cort is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his BA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and an AM at Harvard University, and he served as a professor at Denison University from circa 1993 to 2021.

John F. Richards was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of New Hampshire and UC Berkeley, and he held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (circa 1968–1977) and Duke University (circa 1977–2007).

John Faithfull Fleet was an Indologist and historian who attended Merchant Taylors' School and University College London. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1865–1897), as Epigraphist to the Government of India (1883–1886), and as a Fellow at Bombay University.

Specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, John Gombojab Hangin studied at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana University. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and was full professor at Indiana University (1965–1989).

Religious studies scholar John Grim earned his PhD at Fordham University under Thomas Berry. He has held positions as Professor of Religion at Bucknell University (attested 2005) and Senior Lecturer and Research Scholar at Yale University.
John Henry Hutton was an Indologist and historian. He was educated at Chigwell School and Worcester College, Oxford, and served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1909 to 1936.

John Henry Wright was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated at Dartmouth and Leipzig under Georg Curtius, he held professorial posts at Ohio State, Dartmouth, Johns Hopkins, Harvard, and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens.

John Herbert Harington was an Indologist and historian. He served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of The Asiatic Society, and as an honorary professor at Fort William College (circa 1801–1819).
John Hope studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1740 to 1750 and later held an academic post there from circa 1761 to 1786.

John J. Holder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Harry Krebs and held an Associate Professor post at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018) along with a visiting research appointment at the University of Oxford.

John J. Makransky works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Wisconsin-Madison and guided by traditional teachers and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, he held posts at CIHTS, Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and Boston College (attested 1996–2007).

John James Jones worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Aberystwyth University (circa 1912–1919) and served as Deputy-Keeper of the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales (circa 1926–1957).

John Jorgensen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He has worked as a researcher at Australian National University, taught Japanese Studies at Griffith University, and served as a Senior Research Associate at La Trobe University (attested 2019).
